look_here_first: WITCHGRASS: Warm-season HAIRY ANNUAL. Find distinct coarse/papillose-based hairs along the sheaths and nodes BELOW an enormous airy irregular many-branch panicle. The ripe ~2–4 mm spikelets sit at tips of extraordinarily slender stems. Confirm annual fibrous rootstock and one measured spikelet with shorter lower glume. Seedhead shape alone will NOT distinguish similarly open Panicum grasses.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew/POWO accepts Panicum capillare, describes it as an annual, and lists Texas in its native range. Hagenbuch & Lemke explicitly record Hays County (Breckenridge 518, SWT). UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed Williamson County treatment. USDA ARS Biocollections specimen NA0083935 records Bell County, Texas, Belton Dam Site.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Occurrence is not treated as nativity; introduced records do not count toward the three-county native threshold.

P. hallii = smaller stiff blue-green perennial bunch; P. coloratum = introduced African perennial tough knotty tuft; P. virgatum = larger rhizomatous switchgrass with a white blade-base collar-hair triangle. Witchgrass alone is the hairy annual with huge diffuse panicle.
Examine the same plant's crown, collar and mature spikelet with a millimeter scale before assigning difficult specimens.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Panicum hallii: Witchgrass is annual, hairy, and has a huge diffuse panicle; Hall's is a perennial glaucous bunchgrass with a smaller stiff-branched panicle. Dichanthelium spp.: Witchgrass is annual and lacks the characteristic spring/fall rosette-grass flowering pattern.

measured_reproductive_finalization_20261.look_here_first: WITCHGRASS: verify a fibrous-rooted hairy ANNUAL with swollen-based sheath hairs and a huge airy panicle; confirm solitary 1.9–4 mm mature spikelets, a lower glume only 1/3–1/2 the spikelet, a near-full-length upper glume and a shiny hardened fertile upper floret. A detached tumblehead or purple color alone is not diagnostic.
crew_steps: 1. Trace a flowering culm to its fibrous annual root crown. No rhizomes/stolons in AusGrass; avoid using detached tumbling panicles as proof.
2. At the actual blade–sheath junction, expose the short membranous CILIATE ligule. FNA describes 0.5–1.5 mm marginal cilia; do not confuse stem-node beard or sheath hairs with ligule.
3. Check rough, tubercle-based sheath hairs and hairy nodes under 10–20×. Hair bases need actual magnified pixels, not inferred arrows.
4. Follow the widely spreading 13–50 cm panicle to capillary branches ending in solitary pedicelled spikelets; mature head may break free.
5. Measure several intact ripe spikelets with 1-mm scale: FNA 1.9–4 mm, Kew 1.8–2.5 mm, AusGrass 1.8–3.3 mm; ranges differ by treatment.
6. Dissect one spikelet: small lower glume (1/3–1/2 spikelet), upper glume near full length, lower sterile floret/lemma, then a smaller hardened shiny fertile upper lemma and its palea.
7. Verify no projecting fertile-lemma awn; the sterile lower lemma may have a minute mucro. Compare rootstock, collar and mature spikelet with P. hallii, P. virgatum and P. coloratum.

measured_structures.habit: Annual, tufted, nonrhizomatous; Kew culms 20–80 cm; FNA 15–130 cm. Nodes bearded; sheaths hispid with tubercle-based hairs.
measured_structures.ligule: Membranous with marginal cilia; FNA cilia 0.5–1.5 mm, NZ flora 1–2 mm total ligule. Auricles absent in AusGrass. These are not interchangeable measurements.
measured_structures.panicle: Diffuse 13–50 cm (FNA) or 15–50 cm (Kew); spreading fine branches, can disarticulate as tumblehead.
measured_structures.spikelet: Solitary pedicelled, FNA 1.9–4 mm, Kew 1.8–2.5 mm, AusGrass 1.8–3.3 mm; no species/variety conclusion from range alone.
measured_structures.lower_glume: 1/3–1/2 spikelet; AusGrass 0.9–1.1 mm, 3–5 veins; FNA 1–3 veins, Kew 3 veins.
measured_structures.upper_glume: Approximately spikelet length; FNA 1.8–3.1 mm, 7–9 veins; AusGrass 2–3.3 mm, 5–9 veins; Kew 5–7 veins.
measured_structures.sterile_lemma: Lower sterile floret lemma FNA 1.9–3 mm, AusGrass 2–3.4 mm, 5–7 veins; sterile palea present/reduced depending treatment.
measured_structures.fertile_lemma_palea: Upper fertile lemma hardened, shiny, inrolled margins, AusGrass 1.5–2 mm; palea enclosed and hardened. No long fertile lemma awn; lower sterile lemma can be minutely mucronate.
measured_structures.evidence_scope: All measurements from published treatments; no current gallery image independently supplies calibrated ligule or glume/lemma dimensions.

lookalikes: Panicum hallii — perennial glaucous basal bunch with old curled blades and smaller, stiffer panicle; root crown and spikelets decide.
Panicum virgatum — robust rhizomatous perennial switchgrass; a white collar hair triangle alone is not sufficient.
Panicum coloratum — introduced perennial with persistent knotty crown, potentially open panicle; preserve its existing introduced-range guardrail.
Dichanthelium spp. — perennial rosette grasses with seasonal flowering forms; do not decide from one open head.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Witchgrass: airy panicle, hairy sheath, then real spikelet parts
steps: Start with the Matt Lavin whole diffuse-panicle image (gallery panel 3). Identify long slender branches and small distant spikelets without counting glumes from this scale.
Use Harry Rose's same-species foliage/culm view (panel 4) followed by Matt Lavin's hairy sheath/collar-region view (panel 5). The TRUE ligule is not yet clearly isolated or measured.

Study Stefan.lefnaer's original labelled spikelet dissection (panel 2): glumes, sterile versus fertile lemmas, and fertile palea. These are photographer-labelled source parts, not new assistant arrows or a vouchered same-plant Texas collection.
Compare the physical CC0 tiny spikelet photo (panel 1) with the DIFFERENT SPECIES Panicum hallii photograph (panel 6); never transfer photo-derived claims between the two species.
For a finished local card, photograph a rooted entire annual, an opened true ligule with 1-mm bar, and intact/dissected mature spikelets from the SAME determined Texas individual.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Two actual JPEGs are archived in GitHub; four source photos remain remote-only. Do not claim complete physical archive or a measured ligule. Existing labelled external dissection is useful but not a Hays County same-plant voucher.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · HUGE AIRY HEAD, HAIRY ANNUAL
field_id_short_tiles.short: LOOK HERE FIRST: broad diffuse panicle plus coarse swollen-based hairs on sheath and nodes
field_id_short_tiles.details: Witchgrass is a warm-season fibrous-rooted ANNUAL, not a rhizomatous perennial. Published diffuse panicles ~13–50 cm, often breaking loose when ripe. Actual species panicle panel 3 and hairy-sheath panel 5 are useful, but neither proves a rooted annual or magnified tubercle-based hair origins. Never ID from a detached tumblehead alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ACTUAL HABIT PHOTO — ROOTED ANNUAL/Hair-base MACRO MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · SHORT CILIATE MEMBRANOUS LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Expose the TRUE blade–sheath junction, not the long sheath or node hairs
field_id_short_tiles.details: The ligule is a short membrane with marginal cilia; FNA reports cilia ~0.5–1.5 mm, while other floras give ~1–2 mm for the total ligule. Those are different structures and must not be combined. Auricles absent. Current hairy collar photo does not isolate the membrane edge at 1-mm scale.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · SOLITARY TINY MATURE SPIKELETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Individual spikelets ~1.9–4 mm (FNA), not a cluster of awned florets
field_id_short_tiles.details: Spikelets sit singly at tips of capillary branches; published size ranges vary (Kew ~1.8–2.5 mm, AusGrass ~1.8–3.3 mm). Measure several ripe spikelets with a 1-mm ruler rather than identifying from panicle width or purple color. Existing photo panel 1 shows a real small spikelet but not a Texas same-plant calibrated series.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — SAME-PLANT MATURE SPIKELET WITH 1-MM SCALE

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · SHORT LOWER, LONG UPPER GLUME
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower glume only ~⅓–½ spikelet; upper glume approaches spikelet length
field_id_short_tiles.details: AusGrass lower glume ~0.9–1.1 mm with 3–5 veins; FNA reports 1–3 veins. Upper glume ~1.8–3.1 mm (FNA) or ~2–3.3 mm (AusGrass), with variable 5–9 veins. These treatment ranges are not measurements of existing images. Photographer-labelled dissection panel 2 teaches glume position but needs locally matched, scaled anatomy.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · SHINY FERTILE LEMMA, NO LONG AWN
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower sterile lemma encloses an upper hard shiny fertile floret and palea
field_id_short_tiles.details: Lower sterile lemma commonly ~1.9–3 mm (FNA); upper fertile lemma ~1.5–2 mm in AusGrass, hardened with inrolled margins and enclosed palea. A minute sterile-lemma mucro is possible, but the fertile lemma lacks a projecting long awn. Do not mistake a pointed scale tip for a long awn or infer fine measurements from remote overview panels.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — MEASURED OPENED SPIKELET AND FERTILE FLORET

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · CHECK ROOTSTOCK BEFORE REMOVAL
field_id_short_tiles.short: Separate hairy annual witchgrass from perennial Hall's panicgrass, switchgrass and kleingrass
field_id_short_tiles.details: Native P. hallii is a glaucous perennial with a tighter, smaller bunch; native P. virgatum is a robust rhizomatous perennial, not defined by one white collar triangle; introduced P. coloratum has a persistent knotty crown. Perennial Dichanthelium rosettes may also confuse sterile shoots. Panel 6 is a DIFFERENT species (P. hallii), never a second witchgrass photo. Match rooted plants and mature spikelets before action.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD COMPARISON — MATCHED ROOTED PLANTS NEEDED
